decisions.reason: A rye country bread fits the firm's traditional core, costs little to keep in manual production, and has its own page, so persisting is the natural course.
The premium raisin stollen won the Deutsches Brotinstitut gold medal again, which makes it a publicly celebrated flagship the firm would not abandon.
The seeded rye mixed bread builds on established recipes and is visibly presented, and any weak sales can be blamed on normal assortment fluctuation.
The dark malt rye bread is a niche variant, but it is cheap to keep in the range and consistent with the firm's announced traditional direction.
The marzipan stollen is part of the seasonal gift assortment that is central to the firm, and seasonal results are easily attributed to temporary causes.
The ancient grain bread was publicly announced as the firm's newest masterpiece, so this visible commitment strongly favors keeping it.
